issues.legal_issue: A lower court remains bound by a direct Supreme Court decision on the same statutory provision when later decisions of co-equal benches concern different provisions and do not overrule that decision.
material_facts: A Full Bench overruled a Division Bench that had treated an earlier Supreme Court decision construing the same municipal-law provision as no longer binding.

The later Supreme Court decisions relied on by the Division Bench concerned similar provisions in other laws that lacked the non-obstante clause in the provision construed by the earlier direct decision.
The later decisions distinguished, rather than overruled or referred for reconsideration, the earlier direct decision.
issues.conclusion: The earlier direct Supreme Court decision remained binding on the High Court, and the Full Bench was right to overrule the Division Bench.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 141 of the Constitution, a Supreme Court decision directly construing the relevant provision binds the High Court. A co-equal bench cannot overrule an earlier co-equal decision; it may refer the issue to a larger bench. The Court relied on Municipal Corporation, Indore v. Ratna Prabha, Dewan Daulat Rai Kapoor v. New Delhi Municipal Committee, Dr. Balbir Singh v. Municipal Corporation, Delhi, Morvi Municipality v. State of Gujarat, and The Corporation of Calcutta v. Padma Debi.

predicates.special_leave_challenge_to_full_bench_ru: A party sought special leave to challenge a High Court Full Bench ruling that had overruled a Division Bench ruling.
predicates.earlier_direct_supreme_court_decision_on: The Supreme Court had earlier directly construed the same statutory provision at issue before the lower court.
predicates.later_coequal_decisions_concern_differen: Later decisions by co-equal Supreme Court benches concerned provisions in other laws, which differed in a relevant respect from the provision directly construed earlier.
predicates.later_decisions_did_not_overrule_earlier: The later decisions distinguished the earlier decision and did not overrule it or refer it to a larger bench.

issues.definition: When a special leave challenge concerns a lower court's treatment of a direct Supreme Court decision, and later co-equal decisions addressed different provisions without overruling it, the direct decision remains binding on the lower court.

issues.legal_issue: A municipal annual-value provision containing an overriding clause permits reasonable letting value to be determined without applying a statutory standard-rent limit when no standard rent has been fixed and standard-rent fixation does not apply to the building.
material_facts: The provision under consideration deemed annual value to be the reasonable gross annual rent and expressly applied notwithstanding other laws.

The earlier direct decision construed the provision to allow a reasonable-rent criterion without regard to accommodation-control law where no standard rent had been fixed and the building had never been let and was used in circumstances in which standard-rent fixation did not arise.
The Court held that this construction was a reasonably permissible interpretation of the provision.
issues.conclusion: The interpretation that the overriding clause permits reasonable annual value to be determined without a standard-rent limit in those circumstances was a reasonably permissible construction and was not displaced.
issues.legal_principle: Municipal Corporation, Indore v. Ratna Prabha held that a fixed standard rent, absent fraud or collusion, represents reasonable letting value; where no standard rent is fixed and standard-rent fixation does not arise, reasonable rent may be assessed without applying the accommodation-control law. The Court distinguished The Corporation of Calcutta v. Padma Debi because the provision there lacked an overriding clause, and noted that Dewan Daulat Rai Kapoor, Dr. Balbir Singh, and Morvi Municipality distinguished Ratna Prabha on that basis.

rule.if: municipal_annual_value_uses_reasonable_rent and overriding_clause_applies_despite_other_laws and no_standard_rent_fixed and building_never_let and standard_rent_fixation_does_not_apply

predicates.municipal_annual_value_uses_reasonable_r: The applicable municipal rule measures annual value by the reasonable rent the building could be expected to command.
predicates.overriding_clause_applies_despite_other_: The applicable rule states that its annual-value measure applies notwithstanding other laws.
predicates.no_standard_rent_fixed: No standard rent has been fixed for the building.
predicates.building_never_let: The building has never been let.
predicates.standard_rent_fixation_does_not_apply: The building is used in circumstances in which fixing a standard rent does not arise.

issues.definition: If the annual-value rule uses reasonable rent and overrides other laws, and no standard rent is fixed for a never-let building to which standard-rent fixation does not apply, annual value may be based on reasonable rent without a standard-rent limit.

issues.legal_issue: Reconsideration of an established Supreme Court decision requires compelling and substantial reasons, and a merely preferable alternative interpretation is insufficient.
material_facts: The petitioner sought reconsideration of the earlier Supreme Court decision that directly construed the provision.
That decision had governed annual-value assessments in the State for a long time and was based on the overriding clause in the provision.
The Court regarded the earlier interpretation as reasonably permissible and found no compelling reason to reconsider it.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to reconsider the earlier decision because the test for reconsideration was not satisfied.
issues.legal_principle: Under The Keshav Mills Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax, the Court is reluctant to revise an earlier decision unless compelling and substantial reasons make revision necessary in the public interest or for another valid and compelling reason; a view that an alternative interpretation is more reasonable is not, by itself, adequate.

predicates.supreme_court_review_of_its_earlier_deci: A party asked the Supreme Court to reconsider its earlier decision.
predicates.earlier_decision_long_applied: The earlier decision had governed assessments for a long period.
predicates.earlier_view_reasonably_permissible: The Court considered the earlier interpretation a reasonably permissible view of the law.
predicates.no_compelling_substantial_reason_for_rev: The Court found no compelling and substantial reason requiring revision of the earlier decision.

issues.definition: When the Supreme Court is asked to reconsider a long-applied decision that remains a reasonably permissible view and no compelling substantial reason for revision exists, reconsideration is declined.
